title: Part 3 Practice: Relationship with Other Disciplines, Contributions, & Unit Summary

questions.text: How does anthropology relate to other disciplines in the sciences and humanities?
options: A) It has no relationship with other disciplines.
B) It greatly overlaps with other disciplines and borrows theories and data from them.
C) It is completely separate from all other fields.
D) It only borrows from the natural sciences.
questions.correct_answer: B) It greatly overlaps with other disciplines and borrows theories and data from them.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'In terms of subject matter and areas of study, it greatly overlaps with other disciplines... anthropology may borrow theories and data from such and many other disciplines.'

questions.text: What is a key distinction between anthropology and other disciplines?
options: A) Anthropology only studies modern societies.
B) Anthropology studies humankind in its entirety, using a holistic, comparative, and relativistic approach, and emphasizes extended fieldwork.
C) Anthropology is only a biological science.
D) Anthropology does not use any research methods.
questions.correct_answer: B) Anthropology studies humankind in its entirety, using a holistic, comparative, and relativistic approach, and emphasizes extended fieldwork.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Anthropology differs by its broad scope, unique approach, perspective, unit of analysis, and methods.' It studies humankind in its entirety, holistically, comparatively, and relativistic, with extended fieldwork.

questions.text: What does anthropology use as its primary unit of analysis?
options: A) The individual.
B) Culture as an organizing concept.
C) Economic systems.
D) Political parties.
questions.correct_answer: B) Culture as an organizing concept.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'In its unit of analysis, anthropology takes culture as an organizing concept.'

questions.text: According to the module, what is a major contribution of anthropology to scientific understanding?
options: A) It focuses only on Western cultures.
B) It examines all aspects of humanity, for all periods of time, and for all parts of the globe.
C) It only studies fossils.
D) It ignores cultural diversity.
questions.correct_answer: B) It examines all aspects of humanity, for all periods of time, and for all parts of the globe.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Anthropology has carved out for itself the task of examining all aspects of humanity, for all periods of time, and for all parts of the globe.'

questions.text: How does anthropology serve as a corrective tool to deterministic thinking?
options: A) By accepting all cultural perspectives as absolute truths.
B) By counterbalancing oversimplified explanations with broad, comparative evidence from multiple cultures.
C) By ignoring other cultures.
D) By focusing only on one culture.
questions.correct_answer: B) By counterbalancing oversimplified explanations with broad, comparative evidence from multiple cultures.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Its broad, comparative perspective counterbalances oversimplified explanations, concerning all of humanity, based on evidence obtained from a particular cultural world.'

questions.text: What does the phrase 'anthropology holds up a great mirror to man' mean?
options: A) Anthropology only studies physical appearance.
B) Anthropology helps us better understand and appreciate ourselves by exposing us to the cultural variability of the world's diverse peoples.
C) Anthropology is only about looking at fossils.
D) Anthropology is not useful for self-reflection.
questions.correct_answer: B) Anthropology helps us better understand and appreciate ourselves by exposing us to the cultural variability of the world's diverse peoples.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'As Kluckhohn (1944), put it, "anthropology holds up a great mirror to man and lets him look at himself, in this infinite variety."'

questions.text: How does anthropology contribute to fighting prejudice and discrimination?
options: A) By promoting ethnocentrism.
B) By helping us fight against ethnocentrism and promoting a cross-cultural perspective that sees us as part of one human family.
C) By ignoring cultural differences.
D) By focusing only on one culture.
questions.correct_answer: B) By helping us fight against ethnocentrism and promoting a cross-cultural perspective that sees us as part of one human family.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Anthropology promotes a cross-cultural perspective that allows us to see ourselves as part of one human family... It helps us fight against ethnocentrism; the belief that one's own culture and one's own way of life is superior to others.'

questions.text: What skills does anthropology help students acquire for the 21st century?
options: A) Only technical skills.
B) Broad perspective, appreciating other points of view, operating comfortably in ambiguous situations, and working in cross-cultural teams.
C) Only language skills.
D) Only mathematical skills.
questions.correct_answer: B) Broad perspective, appreciating other points of view, operating comfortably in ambiguous situations, and working in cross-cultural teams.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Anthropology helps us acquire skills crucial for living and working in the twenty-first century. These skills include developing a broad perspective, appreciating other points of view, operating comfortably in ambiguous situations, working effectively as part of cross-cultural teams.'

questions.text: What are some practical areas where anthropology is applied to solve problems?
options: A) Only in museums.
B) Environmental change, globalization, poverty, health, education, ethnic conflicts, human rights, and indigenous cultures.
C) Only in archaeology.
D) Only in linguistics.
questions.correct_answer: B) Environmental change, globalization, poverty, health, education, ethnic conflicts, human rights, and indigenous cultures.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'It is often applied in areas of environmental change and development; globalization, culture change, and global inequalities; poverty; health and nutrition; bilingual and multicultural education; ethnic and religious conflicts; social justice and human rights; and the survival of indigenous cultures and languages.'

questions.text: What is the fundamental contribution of anthropology summarized in the unit summary?
options: A) Understanding only Western societies.
B) Understanding humanity in all its biological and cultural diversity, past and present, creating global awareness.
C) Preserving cultures in museums.
D) Ignoring cultural differences.
questions.correct_answer: B) Understanding humanity in all its biological and cultural diversity, past and present, creating global awareness.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Understanding humanity in all its biological and cultural diversity, past and present, is the fundamental contribution of anthropology. With its holistic and comparative perspectives, it creates a global awareness and a deep appreciation of humanity's past and present.'
